text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Serbian commodity reserves will purchase in advance up to 1,2 million tonnes of wheat, of which 192,900 tonnes as barter and 1,007,000 through wheat selling forward contracts, the government decided at its session Wednesday.

- The federal government decided to end daylight savings time on October 27, when the clock will be moved back one hour, to adjust to EU regulations. It had previously announced the time would change on the last Sunday of September.
- Serbian textile industry output on the rise and exports by end of the year expected to reach $40 million, the Serbian government said Wednesday.

- Conditions have been met for Yugoslavia's joining the International Securities Association, said federal minister without portfolio Vuk Ognjanovic on return from the annual Association meeting in Montreal.
- Vojvodina province scheduled parliamentary elections for November 3, the same day as federal and local elections.
- Bosnian Serb republic acting president Biljana Plavsic says the Serbs will not accept preliminary election results if noted irregularities are not remedied.

- Bosnia will have a central bank which is independent of government and state institutions with two members of the federation and one from the Bosnian Serb Republic in its board of directors, said present Bosnian Central bank governor Kasim Omerovic.
- Federal election commission earmarks 10 million dinars for the organisation of November 3 elections.

- One of Yugoslavia's strategic goals is joining the Council of Europe which would remove obstacles to its becoming part of European integration trends, said federal justice minister Vladimir Krivokapic.
- U.N. security council waiting for report of High Representative to Bosnia Carl Bildt on regularity of Bosnia elections to decide about lifting of Yugoslav sanctions.
- The Serbian trade ministry says it is not aware that electricity prices will go up and it is the one which has to approve the price hikes.
